title: One Plan per Listing: How Host Damage Protection (HostCover) Is Held
content:
**Host Damage Protection (HostCover) is held per listing.** Each listing carries exactly one plan that is pending activation or active at a time. A host with several listings holds several plans, and each plan has its own HostCover level, its own limits, its own plan year and its own claims. There is no cap on the number of plans a host holds.

HostCover Essential is enrolled automatically when a listing is first published. Choosing a paid level changes that plan's level rather than opening a second plan.

## Put another way

| Situation | What the records show |
|---|---|
| A host with one published listing | one plan, on that listing |
| A host with five published listings | five plans, one per listing, each with its own level, limits, plan year and claims |
| A host who chooses a paid level for a listing | the same plan on that listing, now at the paid level |

## Questions this rule answers

**Can one listing carry two plans that are both active?** No. A listing carries exactly one plan that is pending activation or active at a time.

**Do two listings of the same host share one set of limits?** No. Each plan has its own limits and its own plan year, so the claims on one listing's plan do not use up the limits of another listing's plan.

**Is there a ceiling on how many HostCover plans one host may hold?** No; there is no cap on the number of plans a host holds.
